description: Golden graph and query truth snapshot for the B-7 end-to-end corpus gate. B-7 diffs a live run against this file. Update this file under review when intentional graph behaviour changes; never update silently. `corpus_id` is a stable identifier (its historical `-20repo` suffix is not a live count); `corpus_composition.git_repos` is the authoritative repository count.
tolerance_policy: count ranges are [min, max] inclusive; a live run outside the range fails B-7(b). required_correlations assertions must all pass; a missing edge fails B-7(b). query_shapes define required response fields; a missing field fails B-7(c).

Cross-repo Repository DEPENDS_ON Repository edges exist; confirms the B-13 fix — repo_dependency shared_projection_intents drained correctly

At least one AtlantisProject MANAGES a Directory; confirms the atlantis.yaml project-to-Terraform-dir governance edge formed for the terraform_comprehensive fixture

At least one Function HANDLES_ROUTE an Endpoint; confirms the api-svc Flask route handlers bound to their Endpoint nodes (same fixture as rc-2 RUNS_IN; code-path edge, no new cassette)
A Function CALLS another Function; the code call graph projected from the comprehensive code fixtures.
A Class INHERITS another Class; class hierarchy projected from the code fixtures.
A Function REFERENCES a Struct; symbol reference projected from the Go fixtures.
A Repository DEFINES a Workload; workload definition projected from in-repo deploy manifests.
A Function INSTANTIATES a Class; construction edge projected from the code fixtures.
A WorkloadInstance is an INSTANCE_OF a Workload; runtime instance correlation (workload materialization, same machinery as rc-2).
A Workload EXPOSES_ENDPOINT an Endpoint; runtime endpoint exposure (workload materialization, same machinery as rc-2/rc-8).
A WorkloadInstance RUNS_ON a Platform; runtime placement correlation (workload materialization).
A Repository DEPLOYS_FROM another Repository; deployment-source correlation (same deployable machinery as rc-1).

#5441 P1 finding 3 regression guard: the helm_argocd_platform fixture's application.yaml declares source.targetRevision: v1.4.0 pointing at the in-corpus deployable-source repository (github.com/acme/deployable-source.git), which the relationships engine emits as ARGOCD_APPLICATION_SOURCE evidence resolving a DEPLOYS_FROM edge. DEPLOYS_FROM is a tool-agnostic edge also emitted by Kustomize (rc-29) and a Helm chart dependency (rc-34), so this correlation filters on evidence_kinds=[ARGOCD_APPLICATION_SOURCE] to isolate the ArgoCD deployment-source verb, and additionally requires the edge to carry a non-empty source_revision property -- the exact regression this issue fixed: buildResolvedEdgeIntentRow previously read the wrong Details map and always wrote source_revision as "" for every ArgoCD-sourced edge in production. The count and the property are both provably zero/empty without the fix.

#5434 namespace environment-alias binding, closed bound (both a floor and a ceiling, mirroring sl-dart-calls-recursion's pattern): the cassette carries exactly 2 kubernetes_live.namespace facts -- payments-prod, labeled environment=prod (a recognized token), and default, labeled environment=misc-team (a RECOGNIZED label key with an UNRECOGNIZED value -- not IsKnownToken -- so it stays environment-unbound). minimum_count=1 is non-vacuous: it is provably zero without the payments-prod fact's binding logic running (KubernetesNamespaceMaterializationHandler / namespaceEnvironmentFromLabels), proving the POSITIVE case -- an alias-recognized label binds a TARGETS_ENVIRONMENT edge to a canonical Environment node. maximum_count=1 is the NEGATIVE regression anchor and now genuinely exercises the environment.IsKnownToken guard (codex review finding P2, #5434): the prior default fixture carried NO environment-ish label key at all, so it stayed unbound regardless of the guard and the ceiling passed vacuously even with IsKnownToken removed. With a recognized key (environment) but an unrecognized value (misc-team), removing IsKnownToken from namespaceEnvironmentFromLabels would canonicalize and bind default too, pushing this count to 2 and failing the ceiling; the guard in place keeps it unbound and the count at 1. from_label/relationship/to_label alone isolate the producer: no other domain writes a TARGETS_ENVIRONMENT edge FROM a KubernetesNamespace node.

#5441 P1 finding 3 regression guard: USES_MODULE had zero golden-corpus coverage before this fix. The terraform_comprehensive fixture's modules.tf eks module previously declared source = git::https://github.com/example/terraform-aws-eks.git?ref=v1.0.0, an org not in the 20-repo catalog, so it never resolved to a real edge -- exactly the same class of gap that let source_revision (rc-156) sit uncovered before the live gate caught it. Repointed at the in-corpus deployable-source repository (source = git::https://github.com/acme/deployable-source.git?ref=v1.0.0) so the module-source pin is observable end to end: the relationships engine emits TERRAFORM_MODULE_SOURCE evidence resolving a USES_MODULE edge, and evidenceFactFirstPartyRefVersion (evidence_edge_fields.go) derives first_party_ref_version from Details["source_ref"] via ExtractTerraformRefPin since Terraform module evidence never sets first_party_ref_version directly (unlike GitHub Actions). The count and the property are both provably zero/empty without the fixture retarget.

Floor raised 1->3 by #5444 (broadened environment detection beyond path regexes): before #5444 only workload-instance:deployable-config:prod produced this edge (count=1, empirically verified on origin/main e15b3089c with this exact 25-repo corpus). #5444 reads kustomize-deployable-overlay's kustomization.yaml namespace:production (kustomize_overlays[].namespace, alias-canonicalized to prod) into deploymentEnvironments, which the deployable-source candidate's DeploymentRepoIDs=[kustomize-deployable-overlay] resolves into a NEW workload-instance:deployable-source:prod carrying two more DEPLOYMENT_SOURCE edges (to kustomize-deployable-overlay and to its own deployable-config-app dependency), for a total of 3 (empirically verified on branch 5444-broaden-env-detection). required_nodes.description: #5820 P2 review finding: rc-168 only asserted the PackageArtifact node and HAS_ARTIFACT edge exist, which a live projection that creates both but omits or miswrites `hashes` would still satisfy -- and this feature exists specifically to preserve per-artifact digests. This asserts the EXACT `hashes` VALUE, not just presence. The package_registry supply-chain-demo cassette's github.com/acme/lib-common@1.0.0 package_artifact fact carries hashes {sha256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b85, sha512: cf83e1357eefb8bdf1542850d66d8007d620e4050b5715dc83f4a921d36ce9ce47d0d13c5d85f2b0ff8318d2877eec2f63b931bd47417a81a538327af927da3}; packageRegistryHashPairs (go/internal/storage/cypher/package_registry_artifact_writer.go) flattens it into a sorted algorithm:digest string list on the graph node (Cypher properties cannot hold a nested map). `hashes` is a LIST-typed property: boltPropertyString/ListNodeProperty join a Bolt list property's elements with '|' (#5820 fix; without it this assertion would be unconditionally red on a live run regardless of writer correctness) so the joined value can be pinned exactly via allowed_node_property_values. A writer that omits hashes, drops a digest, or corrupts a digest fails this assertion even though rc-168's node/edge existence check would still pass.

A writer that omits event_type or corrupts it fails this assertion even though rc-169's node/edge existence check would still pass.

Dart's call extractor (go/internal/parser/dart/calls.go) was a raw byte-scanner that could not distinguish a declaration header from a call site, recording every function/method/constructor declaration in the corpus as a spurious self-loop CALLS edge (issue #5332). Dart was not staged in the golden corpus, so that corruption class shipped with no durable end-to-end gate (issue #5349). The bound is closed on BOTH sides, not a floor: below 2 means genuine recursion was dropped; above 2 means the #5332 declaration-vs-call-site bug regressed (every one of the fixture's other declarations — DeclarationOnlyWidget's 2 constructors + getter + setter + method, GeoPoint's named constructor, mutualPing/mutualPong, identityFn, LineBuffer.append — would each contribute a spurious self-loop). Mutual recursion (mutualPing<->mutualPong) and the named-constructor/generic-args/cascade call shapes in the same fixture are NOT self-loops (caller != callee) and so do not move this count; they instead flow through the existing generic rc-11 Function-CALLS-Function floor.

execute_language_query.description: MCP tool coverage shape for execute_language_query; asserted live through the MCP tool layer and kept in lockstep with ReadOnlyTools(). #5761 F5: source_backend is a required field (writeLanguageQueryResult has emitted it on every response since #5761) and minimum_results is non-vacuous, mirroring investigate_import_dependencies' #5691 fix above. The shape deliberately sends no repo_id: repo_id in the graph is an opaque generated id (repository:r_8477a002 in this corpus), not a human repo name, so filtering by a readable name matched zero rows and made minimum_results unsatisfiable -- the golden-corpus-gate run that caught this reported '"results" has 0 results, want >= 1'. Without the filter the corpus carries 44 language=go Function entities, so a silently-empty read now fails this gate. This shape does not pin truth.basis, and not because no other shape pins it -- 11 shapes here do. The constraint is that minimum_results (results_field: results) requires Envelope: false for top-level array counting, while pinning truth.basis via required_json_values requires Envelope: true; snapshot.go's contract makes the two mutually exclusive, so truth.basis stays unpinned on purpose. source_backend is pinned to "graph" via required_json_values, so a regression that mis-attributes a content-served row keeps this gate red rather than green. The literal was measured, not guessed: the gate was run with --keep and eshu-api started against the retained stack, and this exact request (language=go, entity_type=Function, limit=10) returned source_backend=graph with truth.basis=authoritative_graph and truth.level=exact -- content enrichment merges nothing for these rows, so the read is pure graph. The gate itself reports only pass/fail and never echoes response bodies, and a value mismatch prints the expected value rather than the observed one, so guessing a literal here would have been unfalsifiable from gate output alone.

list_supply_chain_impact_findings.description: MCP tool coverage shape for list_supply_chain_impact_findings; asserted live through the MCP tool layer and kept in lockstep with ReadOnlyTools(). #5463 flips this floor from the prior vacuous CVE-2026-00000/minimum_results:0 to the NEW Debian OS-package scan-tier chain (CVE-2026-00010, minimum_results:1): the finding is only queryable once the reducer loads vulnerability.os_package cross-scope through the advisory-target reader (#5705) and joins the sibling scanner_worker.analysis from the os_package's own scan scope to stamp subject_digest. subject_digest is omitempty on the finding row, so requiring it under result_item_required_fields plus pinning its exact value under required_json_values proves the digest anchor fired end-to-end — if the os_package load, the scanner-scope join, or the digest stamp regresses, the field drops or the value mismatches and this gate goes red. #5464 strengthens the same floor with a deterministic repository anchor, in two layers. Layer 1: the vulnerabilityintelligence cassette's scanner_worker.analysis now reports the SAME digest the cicdrun cassette's ci.artifact built (sha256:abcdef...ab) instead of a synthetic one -- the correct baseline case this epic's thesis rests on (the image a scanner scans should be the image CI actually built; the mismatch case is #5468) -- which lets classifySupplyChainImpactPackage's os_package branch (supply_chain_impact_index.go) look up reducer_container_image_identity for the resolved digest and anchor RepositoryID from its source_repository_ids, NOT its repository_id (the OCI/container registry's own repository identifier, e.g. oci-registry://ghcr.io/..., a namespace disjoint from every git Repository entity id: joining on it would leave a non-blank RepositoryID permanently unable to reach workload/service/environment context, unit-green and dead in production -- #5464 STEP 1 finding). Layer 2: reducer_container_image_identity has no per-digest canonicalization -- the producer writes one row per triggering scope/ref, and this digest carries 16 rows in the live corpus that disagree on source_repository_ids -- so bestSupplyChainImageIdentitiesByDigest/preferSupplyChainImageIdentity (supply_chain_impact_index_build.go) pick a deterministic winner (prefer an unambiguous single-repository row, tie-break on the lexicographically smallest fact_id) independent of load order, rather than an accidental last-write-wins. Of the digest's 16 rows, only ONE (the ambiguous row this tie-break must reject) names the BUILDING repository (github.com/eshu-hq/supply-chain-demo, repository:r_69256c06 -- the #5423 list_container_image_identities assertion above proves that repo's own source_repository_ids, joined through the cicdrun ci.run against the ociregistry manifest) alongside repository:r_217415d9; the other 15 name ONLY repository:r_217415d9, the deploying repository's own evidence for the same image -- which is what the deterministic winner (unambiguous, fifteen agreeing rows) resolves to and what is pinned here. This floor asserts the repository anchor ONLY; it does NOT assert workload/service/environment reachability. #5464's original design also added a reduce-time stage to backfill runtime context after the anchor resolved, but STEP 0 disproved the invariant that stage depended on: a repository's reducer_workload_identity fact does not reliably commit before that repository's ingestion scope activates -- activation is the projector-stage ack that TRIGGERS the workload_identity follow-up intent asynchronously, not a signal that intent already ran (measured gap ~20-25s across the live corpus, not the negligible window the design assumed), so a reduce-time readiness gate keyed on scope activation would silently reproduce the very bug it was meant to fix, one layer down. That stage was removed; runtime-context reachability is deferred to the query-time runtime-context follow-up (a read-time join of workload/service/environment from the graph), tracked separately from this floor. If the digest alignment or the layer-2 tie-break regresses -- including a regression back to the OCI repository_id or to order-dependent last-write-wins -- the repository_id pin reverts to an unjoinable or wrong value and this gate goes red. The profile argument stays comprehensive to preserve the epic's inclusive OS-package golden-query convention. After #5735 this fixture's exact DPKG affected-version reason also qualifies for precise, so #5736 adds a separate default-profile floor instead of changing this established assertion. #5426 adds the environment half, which nothing in this corpus asserted before: environments and environment_evidence are the BAKED fields applySupplyChainRuntimeContext (go/internal/reducer/supply_chain_impact_runtime.go) writes when a reducer_ci_cd_run_correlation is accepted for the finding, distinct from the read-time-resolved runtime_context above. Both are omitempty on the finding row, so requiring them under result_item_required_fields and pinning environments[]=prod plus environment_evidence.prod=deploy_event asserts the whole join, end to end: the cicdrun cassette's two ci.deployment_event facts resolve the run to the canonical prod token (#5425, the sibling ci-cd/run-correlations HTTP shape), the run's ci.artifact digest equals this finding's subject_digest, and matchingSupplyChainDeployments accepts the correlation rather than rejecting it as provenance-only. That last step is what was broken until #5426: the persisted reducer_container_image_identity row for this digest carried the building repository in source_repository_ids but nothing in build_provenance_repository_ids, because the bare-digest decision #5808 fixed loses the shared stable fact key to the deploying repository's explicit-image-reference decision, and applyCIRunDigestRevision (go/internal/reducer/container_image_identity_registry.go) copied only the weaker field onto the winner. cicdImageMatchesForRepository then had no key to narrow the digest's 16 identity rows, the correlation landed ambiguous + provenance_only, and the finding recorded "deployment evidence provenance-only" in missing_evidence with an empty environments list. Regressing any link -- the build-provenance propagation, the repo narrowing, the deployment-event environment, or the acceptance filter -- drops one of these two fields and reds this gate. The pin is one-sided by measurement, not by choice: prod is the only environment any accepted deployment carries in this corpus, so there is no declared-tier finding value to assert alongside it. Adding the build-provenance repository to this row does NOT move the repository_id pin above: supplyChainImageIdentityAnchorTier reads source_repository_ids FIRST, and the CI scope's row names two repositories there, so the new build provenance moves that row from tier C (unresolvable) up to tier B (resolvable only via its own build provenance) and can never reach tier A -- while the fifteen agreeing deploy-only rows stay at tier A, and tier A never loses to tier B (#5813). Layer 3 (#5810): the cross-scope CI loader that lets a repository-scoped intent see ci.run/ci.artifact facts for DERIVED_FROM (rc-170) is owner-gated (loadActiveContainerImageCIFacts/filterContainerImageCIFactsForOwner, container_image_identity_ci_loader.go) -- a repository-scoped intent admits only CI facts whose run names its OWN repository, and a non-repository scope admits none cross-scope. Unfiltered, the cicdrun cassette's digest-matched ci.run (repository:r_69256c06, the BUILDING repository) was folded into every refreshing scope's rows for this digest, ambiguating all fifteen deploy-only rows out of the layer-2 unambiguous tier and flipping this pin to the builder (the live gate failure: required JSON value findings[].repository_id did not equal repository:r_217415d9). That flip was adjudicated and rejected on the #5810 branch: this field is the runtime-joinable impact anchor (matchingSupplyChainWorkloads/Services/DeploymentLanes join it by exact equality, and the deploying repository is the one that reaches workload/service/environment context -- the builder joins nothing here), #5817's merged review deliberately kept this exact pin for this exact digest, and re-anchoring impact findings to the builder is a semantic redefinition of the finding that needs owner sign-off, not a side effect a lineage loader may impose. No build truth is lost by keeping the pin: the builder attribution stays fully asserted on its own surfaces -- the #5423 list_container_image_identities floor above (source_repository_id=repository:r_69256c06), rc-165 BUILT_FROM, and rc-170 DERIVED_FROM. If the owner filter regresses and foreign CI provenance reaches the deploying repository's rows again, this pin flips to the builder (or blanks, under the pre-symmetrize shape) and this gate goes red either way -- the assertion stays non-vacuous for both historical failure modes.

GET /api/v0/ci-cd/run-correlations?envir.description: Exact build-artifact and deploy-time environment truth for GitHub Actions run 5150 in the supply-chain-demo corpus (#5425, #5822, #5770). The cassette now places two ci.run facts plus run 5150's deployment events in generation 1 and only run 5150's ci.artifact in generation 2. The later artifact digest equals the OCI manifest digest, so this minimum_results:1 object match fails if the artifact-only intent, retained run/deployment lookup, source-snapshot rebuild, or active-generation publication regresses. The separate run-5151 assertion proves the same rebuild keeps the unaffected sibling visible even when generation 1 correlation work was superseded before publication. The cassette's independent same-generation GitLab container_image_identity row carries repository:r_69256c06 in build_provenance_repository_ids, so cicdImageMatchesForRepository narrows the shared digest set to one build-owned identity and classifyCICDRunEvidence must publish outcome=exact with canonical_writes=1. This was not deterministic under #5822's original unordered replay: the CI/CD consumer could finish derived before the cross-scope identity row became active. The durable producer-completion chain now commits an identity completion event atomically with its reducer ACK, reopens or dirties the current CI/CD consumer, and drains every completion event before query truth, so this exact row is the regression floor for that ordering contract. Provider and run filters isolate the authored run, and required_json_object_matches binds every expected value to that same returned object; independent path checks could otherwise pass from different rows while run 5150 remained derived. The row also carries two ci.deployment_event status transitions whose sha equals the run commit, resolving environment=prod with environment_evidence=deploy_event after the history read reloads them by commit. The cassette uses the provider token production and the reducer canonicalizes it to prod; pinning the canonical value prevents a raw-provider regression. Container_image_identity remains the digest-backed identity writer, while #5830 adds a distinct workflow-image-owned BUILT_FROM assertion under evidence_source=reducer/ci-cd-run-correlation/workflow-image; this assertion proves the Postgres CI/CD outcome contract directly.

Generation 1 intentionally contains both runs, while generation 2 contains no 5151 fact and the replay queue may supersede generation 1 correlation work before it publishes a derived snapshot. This exact object match therefore fails if the artifact-only handler copies an absent predecessor result or rebuilds only the patched run.
